C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY.Summary:
The narrow payment-integrity bundle the maintainer ordered on 2026-09-12 ("C1, narrow"). Three live findings are its Problem, and it settles them without growing the findings genre: it deletes the one remaining prose payment path, records the two payments whose payers have no row, and mints its own row to pay the third at the close.
**F197, the prose path.** `derivePayerMap` in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` mints payments by two routes: the `<Pays>` cell of a chartered-or-historical row whose name is an archive directory, and a second pass, `closedWithTokens(row.statusText)`, that mints every `F`-token in a "Closed with" sentence of such a row's `<StatusText>`. F197 named two prose paths; the archived-`spec.xml` pass is already gone (`PAID_FINDING_RE` is defined and used nowhere in `src/` or `scripts/` code; measured 2026-09-12, the name has exactly two occurrences, both fixture data — `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/input/findings.xml:7605` and `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/findings.xml:7523`, a captured finding body quoting it), so the remaining path is `closedWithTokens`. The ruling is narrow: delete it, and declare in the three rows' `<Pays>` every payment it currently mints, so the re-derivation is byte-identical. Measured with the shipped `derivePayerMap` over the real archive (93 directories) and both registry layers (12 live + 50 retired rows): the full map mints 93 tokens, the `Pays`-only map 84, and the nine prose-only tokens are `F100 F101 F102 F103 F104 F105` (`C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE`), `F112 F113` (`C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT`) and `F125` (`C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND`). Driven with the prose loop removed and the nine declared: the map holds 93 of the 93 production tokens with every payer equal, plus this bundle's own new payments — no production token lost, no payer changed.
**F198, a settled finding with no payer.** Its headline is history: `registry-retired.xml` carries a `kind="historical"` row named `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` whose `<Pays>` is `F172`, and `F172` is retired with `<PaidBy>C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2</PaidBy>`. What is still owed is F198's own payment, and the bundle that did the work — `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` (PR #81), whose own Problem measured the rowless population F198 demanded (55 archived bundles with no row in either layer) and whose Summary names the `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` row it wrote — has zero rows in either layer. The house form for exactly that case is a historical row; this is one, born live in `registry.xml` and moved by the same execution wave's `--retire`.
**F185, a fix with no row.** The explicit timeout landed in `src/grace-context.test.ts` as `}, 30_000);` at line 559, in commit `1896592` (PR #75, the `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` merge), as a post-archive commit inside that bundle's PR. That bundle's chartered row already exists, retired; `F185` is appended to its `<Pays>`, with `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2`'s correction of the retired `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS` row as the precedent for editing a retired row.
**Retirement timing is this bundle's trap, and it is sequenced, not discovered.** `F185` and `F198` name already-archived bundles, so both are eligible the moment their payments exist, and the shipped validator exits 1 until `--retire` moves them — driven: the pre-move tree reds exactly `F185` (`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`), `F198` (`C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`) and the born-live `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` row, and one `--retire` reports `moved 3`. This bundle's own row pays `F197` only at the close, when its name becomes an archive directory — driven: the close's `--retire` reports `moved 2` (`F197` and the row). Every committed point validates; the mid-bundle red is a working-tree state, never a commit `validate:ci` can see.
**Two suite repairs are forced and were found by driving, not by reading the brief.** The shipped payer-derivation baseline needs `F185`, `F198` and `F197` in its `bundleMinted` extension, and the shipped `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY` production clamp test — a duplicate under a false name: it reduces to `base + headroom = ceiling` and `base = newlineCount`, exactly what the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots-invariant tripwire already asserts for all four roots, while its title claims a clamp it does not assert (driven: its "headroom below `7 x` median" clause is false after this bundle's moves — headroom 249 against a product of 238 mid-bundle, 266 against 238 post-close). The duplicate test is deleted, the tripwire is named as the carrier of the two relations, and the clamp behaviour stays with the synthetic `--retire` fixtures. With the `bundleMinted` extension and the deletion, the suite is driven 100 pass / 0 fail at the post-close state. The deleted test's defect is staged as `F244`; this bundle repairs it, and `F244`'s payment is recorded at its flush by appending `F244` to this bundle's retired row — the retired-row append this spec establishes for `F185`.
C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY.Problem:
Three live findings, measured at the authoring commit `af0f721b5157f9598fb679736e33d8819cb0400a` (branch `c-payment-integrity`, tree clean, `bun run validate:ci` exit 0).
`F197` (measured 2026-09-08 at `54e26d9`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:466-497`) records that payment eligibility can be minted by wording: `closedWithTokens` reads an archived row's `<StatusText>` and mints every `F`-token in a "Closed with" sentence. `F197` named a second prose path — a pass over every archived `spec.xml` — which is already gone. The observed cost is recorded: `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION`'s spec carries a guard clause asserting its own prose contains no sentence matching the payment pattern, a spec defending itself against its own text. The maintainer's ruling is to delete the remaining path and declare its payments in `<Pays>` instead.
`F198` (measured 2026-09-08 at `54e26d9`) records that `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` archived without a registry row, so `F172` could not be paid. That half is history: `F172` is retired with `<PaidBy>C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2</PaidBy>` under a historical row. What remains is F198's own payment; its Owner is "the next charter decision", which the maintainer made `C1`. The derivation keys on a row whose name equals an archive directory, so an already-archived payer's row makes the finding eligible on sight.
`F185` (measured 2026-09-06, post-archive of `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`) records a real-repository measurement test with no explicit timeout: `buildTaskSlice` against the live package root inherited Bun's 5000 ms default, the archive move took the archive from 69 to 70 directories, and the test ran ~5240 ms. The remedy — `}, 30_000);` on that `it(...)` — could not land inside the closing bundle (its `AC-NO-GRAMMAR` criterion pinned `src/` byte-identical) and landed post-archive in the same PR. That bundle's row exists retired, but names neither `F185` nor the fix.
**A fourth defect, discovered by driving this bundle's own proposed record state and staged as `F244`.** The shipped `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY clamp invariant` test asserts the persisted findings headroom is below `7 x` the median live finding line count. That is a state claim, not an invariant: the ratified arithmetic (`C-ROOT-WINDOW-2`/`-3` — the moved ceiling is `min(previous ceiling, pre-move base + floored headroom)`, with `ceilingBase = findingsBaseRead`) computes the formula ceiling from the pre-move base so a retire frees the moved lines, and when the clamp binds `headroom = 7 x median + lines moved`, which is never below the product. Driven on a whole-repository copy: the mid-bundle move leaves findings `base="7597" headroom="249" ceiling="7846"` against a product of 238, and the close move leaves `base="7569" headroom="266" ceiling="7835"` against 238. This is the expiring-pin class `F225`, `F229`, `F232`, `F237` and `F238` name. The test reduces to the two durable relations the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots-invariant tripwire already carries for all four roots, under a title that claims a clamp it does not assert, so this bundle deletes it (a duplicated assertion is `F116`'s class) and names the tripwire as the carrier. The defect is repaired here; `F244`'s own payment is recorded at `F244`'s flush, when that bundle appends `F244` to this bundle's retired row in `registry-retired.xml` — the retired-row append this spec establishes as lawful for `F185`.

Goals.Goal: Delete the prose payment path and make the derivation byte-identical. In `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, delete `closedWithTokens`, its two private helpers `expandFTokens` and `expandFRange`, and the second loop in `derivePayerMap` that calls `closedWithTokens` — measured at this commit: `closedWithTokens` at `:338`, `expandFTokens` at `:359`, `expandFRange` at `:384`, the call at `:424`, 64 lines of function plus the loop. `derivePayerMap` then mints from `<Pays>` only. In the same change set, declare the nine tokens the path currently mints in their three rows' `<Pays>`: `F100 F101 F102 F103 F104 F105` in `C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE`, `F112 F113` in `C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT`, and `F125` in `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND`, all three in `registry-retired.xml`. The declaration must land before or with the deletion — the deletion alone drops nine tokens from the derivation and reds the baseline test; the declaration alone is byte-neutral because the nine rows are already retired and the `Pays` loop runs first, so the payer is unchanged. The row-invariant tests' StatusText clauses (a row's `<StatusText>` carrying no `F`-token and no "Closed with" sentence) stay as house-form style checks for the rows that carry them; they call no deleted function and pin no payment state.

Record F185's and F198's payments, and mint this bundle's own row. In `registry-retired.xml`, append `[F185](#f185)` to the retired `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` row's `<Pays>`, whose present bytes are `[F180](#f180), [F181](#f181).`; the witness is the timeout at `src/grace-context.test.ts:559`, introduced by `1896592` (PR #75). In `registry.xml`, birth a `kind="historical"` row named `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` with `<Pays>F198</Pays>` in the house form ("This row exists so the derivation can see the payment"), with a present-tree witness: the `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` historical row in `registry-retired.xml` whose `<Pays>` is `F172`, `F172` retired with `<PaidBy>C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2</PaidBy>`, and `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`'s own measured rowless population. Mint this bundle's row `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY`, `status="live"`, `kind="chartered"`, whose `<Pays>` is exactly `F197`, whose `<Charter>` records the mint search (measured below), and whose `<StatusText>` is house-form prose naming no `F`-token and carrying no "Closed with" sentence. After every hand write of a record file, run the shipped `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --rewrite-roots`; never hand-edit a root. Then run the shipped `--retire` in the same execution wave: the born-live historical row and the now-eligible `F185` and `F198` move, `moved 3`, and the committed tree validates. The bundle's own row stays live until the close.

Repair the retirement suite for the state this bundle produces, and add the guard that keeps the prose path dead. In `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`: (a) delete the `closedWithTokens` import and its one direct call site — the `closedWithTokens(statusText)` assertion inside the `C-FLUSH-AND-UNPIN payment invariant` test at `:2503` — and delete the `Closed-with citation reduction` test at `:405`, whose expectation *is* the deleted path's behaviour (it drives the prose path through the validator on an isolated root and asserts `F100`–`F101` eligibility; it calls no function directly), replacing it with a prose-dead guard that asserts the opposite on the same shape: over an isolated archive root, a row named for an archive directory whose `<StatusText>` carries `Closed with F999` and whose `<Pays>` is empty mints nothing, while the same row with `<Pays>F999</Pays>` mints `F999` — the discriminating direction proves the instrument is not vacuously empty; (c) extend the `bundleMinted` map with `F185: "C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY"`, `F198: "C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2"` and `F197: "C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY"`; (d) delete the `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY` production clamp test — its two surviving relations (`base + headroom = ceiling`, `base = newlineCount`) are exactly what the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots-invariant tripwire already asserts for all four roots, and its title claims a clamp it no longer asserts — leaving the clamp behaviour with the existing synthetic `--retire` fixtures. The engine deletion and the suite's prose-path removals land together (the suite will not compile against a deleted export). Every assertion is written payment-invariantly: no token is pinned to a layer or a payment state, and every fixture that locates a holder walks both layers.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier **T1** (module-change shape, the tier `C-FLUSH-TWO-WAVES` chose for the same record-and-suite surface): the record engine's payment derivation, the retirement suite, and this bundle's own artifacts. No graph module is written, no `src/` file is edited, and exactly one `scripts/` production file is edited (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`) beside its suite. Roadmap: `RM-GOVERNED-PATH` (record integrity). Binding live rulings: `D28` and `D28.1` (eligibility is the enforcement and the ceiling the backstop — the mid-bundle red is the enforcement saying the move is due, a declared working-tree state, never a commit `validate:ci` can see; every write lands inside every persisted window); `D30` (scoped, not skirted — the record is this bundle's deliverable; no other dispatch reads or rewrites the record while a record-writing task is in flight, and findings raised while this bundle is open go to `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`); `D27` (nothing is approved unread; ratification is the maintainer's); `D11` (nothing is deferred here — the named NonGoals have owners, not open deferrals); `D38` (bundle ids stay hash-less until the `-N-HASH` builder ships; this bundle supersedes nothing and adds no lineage suffix — the id is the hand-minted legacy `C-<SLUG>` form); `F43` (escape markup as character data — `<`, `>`, `&` — and never paraphrase brackets away). This bundle runs no `ngrace review`, no gate, no cursor or supersede verb, and no commit: the executor authors `spec.xml` at `status="draft"` and stops; the approval write and the close's move are the authority's.

**Windows, measured at this commit, not assumed.** Findings live root `base="7673" headroom="173" ceiling="7846"` with 211 live `<Finding>` children, median element line count 34 under the shipped counting rule (`newlineCount(span) + 1`), `7 x 34 = 238`; rulings `base="1733" headroom="150" ceiling="1883"`; registry `base="12" headroom="14" ceiling="26"` with 12 live rows and 50 retired rows; index `base="273" headroom="23" ceiling="296"` with 376 `<Entry>` children, 273 live. **The nine declarations and the byte-identity they buy.** The three rows are all `status="retired" kind="chartered"` in `registry-retired.xml`, so editing their `<Pays>` cannot change any live finding's eligibility: the nine tokens are all carried by retired findings (measured: `F100`-`F105`, `F112`, `F113` and `F125` each have zero live carriers and one retired carrier). The edit is lawful because the record's registry is the machine-readable current-state surface and the derivation reads both layers; `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2`'s `AC-SWEEP` corrected the retired `C-CODIFY-DECISIONS` row's `<Pays>` and `<Charter>` in place, and this is the same catch-up shape. The declaration's exact shape is the row's existing `<Pays>` with the nine tokens appended, e.g. `C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE` gains `[F100](#f100), [F101](#f101), [F102](#f102), [F103](#f103), [F104](#f104), [F105](#f105)`, `C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT` gains `[F112](#f112), [F113](#f113)`, and `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND` gains `[F125](#f125)`; the citation link form is what the surrounding cells use, and the derivation's tokenizer reads the token either way. `F185` is the tenth appended token, on `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`. The rows' "Closed with" sentences stay in their `<StatusText>` as historical prose; after the deletion they mint nothing, and this spec says so rather than silently editing history out of the record.

**The StatusText rule after the change, decided from the measured population.** Once `closedWithTokens` is deleted, a token mentioned in a row's `<StatusText>` mints nothing, so no validator rule forbidding `F`-tokens in `<StatusText>` is owed — such a rule would protect nothing. Measured across both layers: **14 rows** carry an `F`-token in `<StatusText>` (`C-EFFORT-DEPTH`, `C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE`, `C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT`, `C-SUPERSEDE-VERB`, `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND`, `C-SCOPE-AUDIT-ATTRIBUTION`, `C-AUDIT-001`, `C-IDENT-COVERAGE`, `C-LEDGER-MEMBERSHIP`, `C-PROBE`, `C-DECLARED-WRITES`, `C-RECORDED-DEBT`, `C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY`, `C-FLAG-HONESTY`); only three of them carried a "Closed with" sentence and minted the nine tokens above, and eleven merely mention a token. A general rule would therefore red 14 rows, eleven for a mere mention. The per-row invariant clauses that assert a named row's `<StatusText>` is house-form prose may stay and may be asserted for the new `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row; they are style, not payment law, and no general validator rule is added.

**The committed sequence, and which entries move when.** The plan must sequence the writes so every committed point validates; the mid-bundle red is a working-tree state only. (1) **The record payments and the suite they force.** Land the nine declarations, the `F185` append, the born-live `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` historical row, and the live `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row; run `--rewrite-roots` (registry `14 / 12 / 26`); the shipped validator exits 1 naming exactly `F185` (`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`), `F198` (`C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`) and the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` row; run one `--retire`, which reports `moved 3`; then land the suite repairs the new state forces (`bundleMinted` extension, the clamp-test repair); commit only when `validate:ci` exits 0. Mid-bundle entries that move: `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` (row), `F185`, `F198`. At the close: `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` (row), `F197`. Nothing else in the findings, rulings, registry or index genres moves.

**The clamp-test disposition, and `F244`'s payment route.** The `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY` production test is **deleted**, not repaired. Reduced to its two durable relations (`base + headroom = ceiling`, `base = newlineCount(findings.xml)`) it asserts exactly what the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots-invariant tripwire already asserts for all four roots — a duplicated assertion, `F116`'s class — and the test's title, "`clamp invariant`", claims a clamp it does not assert; keeping a renamed duplicate would need a reason the tripwire does not cover, and there is none. No test then claims a clamp it does not assert. The two relations stay guarded by the tripwire, whose red direction is a mutated copy whose `headroom` no longer sums against its `ceiling`; the suite at the post-close state with the deletion plus the `bundleMinted` extension is driven `100 pass / 0 fail`. `F244`'s payment is not this bundle's row's: `F244` is staged, so no record token exists yet.
